Quran.title: Qur'anic Arabic
Quran.intro: Listen to the imam, then learn each word's meaning, its root, and why it ends in fathah, dammah or kasrah. Explained simply, sourced from named kitabs.
Quran.how_1: Pick an ayah, then click “Start the lesson”. The imam recites the ayah, then the lesson explains each word, step by step. You can pause at any time.
Quran.how_2: Short exercises come up inside the lesson, with no time limit. After that the lesson moves on to the next ayah by itself.
Quran.how_3: Want to read more? Open “Full material for this ayah” under the lesson: each word's card, the exercises and the references.
Quran.p1_body: Every ayah in the lessons is recited by a human reciter, the imam Mishary Alafasy, and every word played one by one is a word recording from Quran.com. The AI voice of the narrator Kang Nandar explains in Indonesian, and voices only parts of words, letters, practice forms and runs of several words that have no word recording.
Quran.p2_body: Every meaning, i'rab note and hadith is quoted from a named kitab or dataset, with its reference.
Quran.p3_body: Explanations are prepared with AI help from named kitabs. This is learning material, not a fatwa: check the references, and ask a teacher when in doubt.
Quran.curriculum_body: The lessons build up step by step: at most {max} new things in each lesson, and what has been learnt is repeated whenever it comes up again. See the order, from the introduction lesson to {last}.
Quran.rumus_body: One short formula for each thing learnt, with an example from the lessons and the kitab sentence it rests on.

Rumus.title: Quick formulas (rumus singkat)
Rumus.description: Quick formulas for basic Arabic grammar: one short formula for each thing learnt, with an example from the lessons and the kitab sentence it rests on.
Rumus.intro_what: The quick formulas are a short summary of each thing learnt at the basic level, to keep at hand while reading. Each formula comes with one example from the lessons.
Rumus.intro_sources: Each formula restates one sentence of the kitab named under it, in the “Basis” part, with its page and a quotation of that sentence. A thing with no kitab sentence that can be quoted has no formula yet.
Rumus.intro_label: AI-assisted, not an authoritative fatwa. These formulas are drawn from the kitab named under them; check the references.
Rumus.intro_with_lesson: The quick formulas complement the full explanation in the lessons and on the Concept pages; they do not replace it.

Credits.title: Sources & licences
Credits.intro: This module is built on the works and data below. We credit each source as its terms require. The recitation of the ayat in the lessons and the word recordings are copied, unaltered, to our server for non-profit educational use, so they play without delay.
Credits.words_body: Every Qur'anic word played on its own, in the lessons and on the Concept pages, is Quran.com's (Quran Foundation) word-by-word recording of that word at its place in the Qur'an. The files are copied, unaltered, to our server for non-profit educational use; only the part of the file that holds the word is played. Their buttons say “Quran.com recording”.
Credits.voice_body: The explanations (ElevenLabs, eleven v3) are made with AI from the voice of the narrator Kang Nandar. The same AI voice (ElevenLabs, multilingual v2) also voices what has no word recording: parts of words (such as bi- or -hum), letters, practice forms not written in the Qur'an, and runs of several words. Their spelling is adjusted where needed so they are read correctly, and every one of those recordings was listened to before it was used. Their buttons say “AI voice”. These are not recordings of the imam.
Credits.recitation_heading: The imam's recitation on the lesson pages
Credits.recitation_body: Every ayah is played from these recordings, with a timing for every word. They come from EveryAyah (everyayah.com) and are copied, unaltered, to our server for non-profit educational use:
Credits.streaming_note: The recordings in the lessons and on the Concept pages play from our server. Only the recitation in the ayah window opened from a “Did you know?” card is still fetched directly from EveryAyah's servers abroad: when you play it, your IP address is visible to them.
Credits.data_versions_body: For technical checks: the version and file fingerprint (sha256) of every dataset the lesson pages use, exactly as recorded when the lessons were built.
Credits.data_versions_ayat: Ayat opened from the “Did you know?” cards
Credits.kosakata_body: Rank, counts, roots and word forms are computed from the Quranic Arabic Corpus 0.4 and the Tanzil text. Ayah translations are from QuranEnc. Word meanings were written with AI (Claude) from the cited ayat, using the QuranEnc and Saheeh International translations, then checked by AI. These meanings do not yet cite a kitab. Each word's sound: Quran.com / Quran Foundation's word-by-word recording of one place where the word occurs in the Qur'an. Unaltered copies are on our server. The tests in the step-by-step path are built by rule from the same data. We only count numbers: how many browsers open each section, how many visits arrive from the main Dakwah-Lens site, and how many times each test is tried and passed, with no name, account or IP address.
